name: Disposition Effect
description: People can become more willing to lock in gains than to realize losses, selling winners too early while holding losers too long. The current gain/loss status of an option distorts exit decisions.
design_relevance_note: Most relevant to fintech, investing, portfolio dashboards, and resale/marketplace tools: how unrealized gains and losses are framed can distort selling decisions even when a more detached strategy would say to act differently.
prevalence_note: A standard named bias in behavioral finance and directly relevant to investing-product design, but not part of generic everyday UX canon outside money products.

findings.description: In an experimental securities-trading task, participants showed the classic disposition-effect asymmetry: they were more willing to realize gains than losses, selling winning assets too early while holding losing assets too long.
findings.source_title: The disposition effect in securities trading: an experimental analysis
